items.abstract: In science, one-dimensional deterministic (i.e., non-random) systems provide the simplest models for processes that evolve over time. Mathematically, these models take the form of one-dimensional difference or differential equations. This chapter presents the basic theory of Benford's law for them. Specifically, it studies conditions under which these models conform to Benford's law by generating Benford sequences and functions, respectively. The first seven sections of the chapter focus on discrete-time systems (i.e., difference equations) because they are somewhat easier to work with explicitly. Once the Benford properties of discrete-time systems are understood, it is straightforward to establish the analogous properties for continuous-time systems (i.e., differential equations), which is done in the chapter's final section.
title: Real-valued Deterministic Processes
